extracted.intended_audience: stand-up comedians developing long-form storytelling material
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing and performing long-form, memoir-style stand-up that centers a single thematic question and uses vulnerability, callbacks, and careful structure to build to an emotional-then-comedic climax.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is there a story the comedian was reluctant to tell?
rubrics_metrics.description: "I always ask people, 'What's the story you don't want to tell anyone?' And, weirdly, that is the story you want to tell on stage."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Material selection criterion: choose a story you are reluctant to tell — the audience can feel the reluctance. Vulnerability creates immediate empathy; the audience senses the cost of disclosure, trust accelerates, and the audience is willing to go to 'different places.' Anti-pattern: choosing safe, glib anecdotes that avoid real stakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is there a clear through-line / theme?
rubrics_metrics.description: Often a single thematic question (sleep, marriage, mortality, swimming); many anecdotes but one through-line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The special should have a unifying question or theme so disparate anecdotes cohere. Memoir-style structure and 'essays with beats' help unify material; evaluate whether each anecdote contributes to the central thematic arc or feels tangential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Are there long-form callbacks?
rubrics_metrics.description: Earlier story elements return and are recontextualized at the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use callback loops where beats introduced early resurface later to click the structure into place for the audience. Effective long-form callbacks reframe prior material rather than merely repeating punchlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Is the structure tight (no padding)?
rubrics_metrics.description: Care and attention to structure, pacing, cohesion; structure tight (no padding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Long-form storytelling requires painstaking structural discipline: trim padding, ensure pacing keeps momentum, and maintain cohesion across sections. Birbiglia emphasizes careful construction — work in smaller chunks, then integrate. Anti-patterns: wandering tangents, filler beats that don't advance theme or character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Does emotional honesty land alongside laughs?
rubrics_metrics.description: Emotionally honest observational humor — doesn't deflect with deflection humor; real feelings present in the room; comedy IS the emotional processing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether vulnerability and genuine feeling coexist with comedic beats. Emotional honesty should feel earned and create empathy without undercutting jokes; the audience should sense authentic risk and emotional cost. Anti-pattern: forced sentimentality or using false vulnerability as a setup for cheap laughs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Iterative development and revision
rubrics_metrics.description: Works in smaller chunks first; painstakingly crafted over months in club and theater sets; revises nightly; tracks changes with color-coded setlists.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate the creator's process and evidence of iterative testing: nightly revisions, tracking what changes, and willingness to discard many jokes ("100 jokes that work" comes from "500 jokes that don't work"). Scoring guidance: favor material with visible evolution and pruning over 'works on first try' drafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specials structure: climactic emotional moment and recontextualizing final laugh
rubrics_metrics.description: Many anecdotes, one through-line; climactic emotional moment near the end; final laugh that recontextualizes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a long-form special, check for an emotional climax late in the set that resolves or deepens the thematic question, followed by a final laugh that reframes earlier material. The arc should move the audience emotionally before delivering a recontextualizing payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance style: hyper-verbal, less physical
rubrics_metrics.description: Long-form storytelling, hyper-verbal. Less reliant on physicality / facial. 'Essays with beats.' Memoir-style structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the material is constructed primarily for verbal narrative and structural beats rather than physical gestures or facial work. This style favors language, pacing, and internal beats; delivery should foreground story and tonal shifts more than physical comedy.
